copy.instagram:
We’ve all been there: 20 tabs open, a pile of PDFs, and a sinking feeling that you’re just summarizing papers instead of actually writing a review. It’s the fastest way to lose marks for ‘lack of critical synthesis.’

Stop writing linear summaries. Instead, build a Matrix. 

Slide 1: The Trap. Writing paper-by-paper creates a 'shopping list' of summaries. It’s boring to read and rarely hits the high-tier marks.

Slide 2: The Matrix. Create a spreadsheet with columns for Author, Methodology, Key Findings, and—most importantly—Thematic Debates. 

Slide 3: The Result. By mapping sources this way, you can spot where authors disagree or where your research gap actually hides. It turns a 20-hour slog into a clean, logical argument.

Want the exact template I used to clear my dissertation? Check the link in my bio to grab it. 

Save this for your next library session so you don’t waste another night staring at a blank screen.

copy.facebook:
I remember the exact moment I realized I was doing my literature review all wrong. I had spent three days summarizing individual papers, only to realize I had zero actual argument. My supervisor’s feedback was brutal: 'Where is the synthesis?'

If you’re feeling the pressure of a looming deadline, stop the 'chaotic method' of writing one summary after another. It’s time to use a Matrix.

Here is how to structure it:
• Columns: Author/Year, Methodology, Key Variables, and Thematic Debates.
• The Goal: Group your sources by theme, not by author. 
• The Outcome: You’ll easily identify contradictions and research gaps—the golden ticket to higher marks.
